claim: The AND mouse is a strain with a transgenic CD4+ T cell TCR.
source: the AND mouse is a strain with a transgenic CD4+ T cell TCR (Kaye et al., 1989)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to Kaye et al., 1989.

claim: The AND TCR recognizes pigeon cytochrome c (PCC) along with synthetic and species-variant cytochrome c oligopeptides.
source: This TCR recognizes pigeon cytochrome c (PCC) along with synthetic and species-variant cytochrome c oligopeptides (Solinger et al., 1979; Rogers and Peptide dose, 1999; Rogers et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: CD4+ T cells follow a digital pattern for each given peptide and dose, appearing either all-on or all-off according to extracellular activation markers such as CD69.
source: As expected, for each given peptide and dose, CD4+ T cells followed a digital pattern, appearing either all-on or all-off according to extracellular activation markers such as CD69 (Figure 1A) and CD25 (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1A and 1B.

claim: Increasing the peptide dose or affinity significantly increased the percent of activated cells in the population.
source: Increasing the peptide dose or affinity significantly increased the percent of activated cells in the population (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1C and 1D.

claim: When comparing across peptides and concentrations, the activation level of the on-state cells varies with both dose and affinity of the stimulation.
source: Gating on CD69+ cells, each different peptide and different dose of a peptide achieved a different amount of CD69 per cell (Figure 1E). Gating on CD25+ cells yields similar results, with varying amounts of CD25 expressed per cell dependent on both the dose and the affinity of the stimulation (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1E and 1F.

claim: While under a given condition the CD4+ T cells were either on or off as per classical digital signaling, when comparing across a panel of conditions, the activation level of the on-state cells is analog with respect to the strength of the TCR signal.
source: Thus, while under a given condition the CD4+ T cells were either on or off as per classical digital signaling, when comparing across a panel of conditions, the activation level of the on-state cells is analog with respect to the strength of the TCR signal.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 1.

claim: A single principal component explained more than 99% of the variance in gene expression changes across the five conditions.
source: A single principal component explained more than 99% of the variance in gene expression changes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The first principal component ranks the samples according to TCR signal strength.
source: The first principal component ranks the samples according to what would be expected based on TCR signal strength and extracellular markers such as CD69 and CD25 (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The 10% of genes contributing the most positive signal to PC1 were increasing in a generally graded manner with TCR signal strength across the samples.
source: The 10% of genes contributing the most positive signal to PC1 were increasing in a generally graded manner with TCR signal strength across the samples, and the 10% of genes contributing the most negative signal were decreasing (Figure 2B; two-tailed p-values based on permutation testing of 2.9e-11 and 1.8e-28, respectively).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2B with statistical significance determined by permutation testing.

claim: Activation signature genes include many genes previously identified as important to CD4+ T cell activation, such as Tbx21 (Tbet), Stat1, and Tnf.
source: Looking more closely at the genes in this group, we see many well-documented immune response genes such as Tbx21 (Tbet), Stat1, and Tnf (Figure 2C), all of which increase in a graded manner along with TCR signal strength at the population level.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Irf4 showed a graded response pattern at the population level across the conditions.
source: Irf4, previously reported to increase in expression in an analog manner downstream of the TCR on a per-cell basis (Man et al., 2013; Nayar, 2014), was also among the activation signature genes, and showed the same graded response pattern at the population level across the conditions (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2D, with citations to previous work.

claim: Gene Ontology analysis yielded several enriched gene categories among the activation signature, including Myc targets, post transcriptional regulation of gene expression, MTORC1 signaling and response to cytokine and regulation of translational initiation.
source: Gene Ontology analysis yielded several enriched gene categories among the activation signature, including Myc targets, post transcriptional regulation of gene expression, MTORC1 signaling and response to cytokine and regulation of translational initiation (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Protein biosynthesis has been previously shown to be increased upon T cell activation.
source: Protein biosynthesis has been previously shown to be increased upon T cell activation, and here we see that many of the genes involved in increasing translational activity are themselves up-regulated in a manner that is proportional to the level of activation across the population (Beretta, 2004; Bjur et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: The graded increase of activation signature genes at the population level corresponded with single-cell increases in CD69 and CD25 protein.
source: The graded increase of activation signature genes at the population level corresponded with single-cell increases in CD69 and CD25 protein, but it was unclear whether the graded response of proteins associated with activation signature genes was generalizable.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 1 and Figure 2.

claim: For proteins that showed increases in mRNA levels reflected at the level of protein, the increases in mRNA resulted in increases both in the frequency of cells responding and in protein levels on a per-cell basis.
source: Not all increases in mRNA levels were reflected at the level of protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), but for those that were, the increases in mRNA resulted in increases both in the frequency of cells responding (data not shown) and in protein levels on a per-cell basis. This is exemplified by the expression of Tbet (Figure 2F), IRF4 (Figure 2G), CD200 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E), Ly6a (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F), and Tnsf11 (RANKL; Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Beta actin mRNA as measured by RNA flow cytometry was constant under each treatment condition.
source: In contrast, beta actin mRNA as measured by this technique was constant under each treatment condition (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: For some mRNAs, in addition to modulating the frequency of responding cells, peptide dose and affinity tune the strength of response to TCR signaling on a per-cell basis.
source: Thus, for some mRNAs, in addition to modulating the frequency of responding cells, peptide dose and affinity tune the strength of response to TCR signaling on a per-cell basis.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The first principal component of CD69+ sorted cells orders the four conditions by increasing TCR signal strength.
source: Across the four treated samples, the first principal component again sorted the conditions according to the relative strength of TCR signaling (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Looking at the genes composing the top 10% of PC1 in CD69+ sorted cells, gene expression patterns largely reflected the same trend, increasing with increasing TCR signal.
source: Looking at the genes composing the top 10% of PC1, we saw, as with the whole-population RNA-seq, that gene expression patterns largely reflected the same trend, increasing with increasing TCR signal (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Genes associated with cell metabolic processes like translation and RNA biosynthesis were enriched in the top 10% of PC1 in CD69+ sorted cells.
source: As with the whole-population data, genes associated with cell metabolic processes like translation and RNA biosynthesis were enriched (Figure 3D), indicating that the expression of genes in key cellular activation pathways increases with increasing TCR signaling on a per-cell basis as well as at the population level.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: There was a group of genes that were near maximally activated in CD69+ cells treated with the low concentration of K99A and exhibited similar expression across all treatment conditions.
source: In contrast to the whole-population data, there was a group of genes that were near maximally activated in CD69+ cells treated with the low concentration of K99A and exhibited similar expression across all treatment conditions. This 'digital' pattern is illustrated in Figure 3E for the 100 most highly induced/most consistently expressed genes and for representative genes in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The digital cluster of genes was enriched for immune signaling terms.
source: GO analysis demonstrated that this digital cluster of genes was enriched for immune signaling terms (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: The graded increase in expression of activation signature genes at the population level is a reflection of both frequency of responding cells and incremental increases in expression levels on a single-cell level for at least a subset of genes, including key cellular metabolism genes.
source: Thus, the graded increase in expression of activation signature genes at the population level is a reflection of both frequency of responding cells and incremental increases in expression levels on a single-cell level for at least a subset of genes, including key cellular metabolism genes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The activation score was able to quantitatively rank conditions within a given experiment set such that activated and naïve CD4+ T cells could be distinguished.
source: We compared samples from several publicly available datasets, and the activation score was able to quantitatively rank conditions within a given experiment set such that activated and naïve CD4+ T cells could be distinguished and further that the effects of various genetic perturbations of CD4+ T cell responses could be observed.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The activation score correctly recapitulated the findings that polarized helper subsets of CD4+ T cells were more pro-inflammatory than unstimulated cells or induced and natural regulatory T cells.
source: For example, the activation score correctly recapitulated the findings that polarized helper subsets of CD4+ T cells were more pro-inflammatory than unstimulated cells or induced and natural regulatory T cells (Wei et al., 2009) (Figure 4B)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4B, with a citation to published work.

claim: At the population level plate-bound anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 induced stronger activation signals than APCs plus antigen.
source: that at the population level plate-bound anti-CD3 and anti-CD28 induced stronger activation signals than APCs plus antigen (Tan et al., 2014) (Figure 4C)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4C, with a citation to published work.

claim: Costimulation was important for achieving higher activation states but checkpoint inhibitors could block this effect.
source: that costimulation was important for achieving higher activation states but checkpoint inhibitors could block this effect (Wakamatsu et al., 2013) (Figure 4D)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4D, with a citation to published work.

claim: Knockout of Trim28, a molecule necessary for optimal IL2 production, diminished CD4+ T cell activation status.
source: that knockout of Trim28, a molecule necessary for optimal IL2 production, diminished CD4+ T cell activation status (Chikuma et al., 2012) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, with a citation to published work.

claim: Acute LCMV infection produced more robust activation in CD4+ T cells than chronic infection.
source: and that acute LCMV infection produced more robust activation in CD4+ T cells than chronic infection (Doering et al., 2012) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, with a citation to published work.

claim: C57BL/6 cells were more activated than most strains, while BALB/c mice were less activated than most strains.
source: As would be predicted by known strain phenotypes, C57BL/6 cells were more activated than most strains, while BALB/c mice were less activated than most strains.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 4E.

claim: The strain with the highest activation score, DBA/2, had top-quartile expression of more than half of the activation signature genes.
source: The strain with the highest activation score, DBA/2, had top-quartile expression of more than half of the activation signature genes (p=7.4e-30 by chi-squared test).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 4E, with statistical significance determined by chi-squared test.

claim: By and large, the H3K4me2-marked regions across the five conditions were very similar.
source: By and large, the H3K4me2-marked regions across the five conditions were very similar (Table 1), with a comparison of tag counts associated with specific genomic regions under no peptide or 1 µM PCC illustrated in Figure 5A.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Table 1 and Figure 5A.

claim: The gene expression and phenotypic changes seen after activation were not due to selection of new signal-dependent enhancers.
source: Thus, the gene expression and phenotypic changes seen after activation were not due to selection of new signal-dependent enhancers.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5A and Table 1.

claim: The top motif among primed enhancers shared by the five conditions was an ETS motif.
source: The top motif was an ETS motif (Figure 5B), capable of being bound by a number of ETS factors that are expressed in CD4+ T cells, including Ets1, Ets2, and Elf1 (Anderson et al., 1999).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5B, with a citation to published work.

claim: Runx factors play an important role in T cell development.
source: Similarly, Runx factors play an important role in T cell development (Wong et al., 2011), and correspondingly the Runx family motif was highly enriched among primed enhancers.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Several known motifs for SDTFs were enriched among the H3K4me2-marked enhancers, including an Interferon Regulatory Factor (IRF) motif.
source: Several known motifs for SDTFs were also enriched among the H3K4me2-marked enhancers (Figure 5C), including an Interferon Regulatory Factor (IRF) motif.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: An AP-1 motif and an NF-κB motif were significantly enriched in primed enhancers.
source: Similarly, an AP-1 motif and an NF-κB motif were significantly enriched in primed enhancers (Figure 5C), corresponding with the fact that TCR signaling greatly increases activity of both of these transcription factors (Huang and Wange, 2004; Rincón and Flavell, 1994).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5C, with citations to published work.

claim: In contrast to H3K4me2, a substantial portion of enhancers exhibited increases in the H3K27Ac activation mark.
source: In contrast to H3K4me2, a substantial portion of enhancers exhibited increases in the H3K27Ac activation mark (Figure 5D, Table 2).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5D and Table 2.

claim: Enhancers that became more active with TCR engagement were highly enriched for both AP-1 and NF-κB motifs.
source: Enhancers that became more active with TCR engagement were highly enriched for both AP-1 and NF-κB motifs (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Enhancers that became more active with TCR engagement were more likely to be proximal to activation signature genes than would be expected at random.
source: Further, this group of enhancers was more likely to be proximal to activation signature genes than would be expected at random (p-value = 2.0e-20 by chi-squared test).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5E, with statistical significance determined by chi-squared test.

claim: There was an increase in H3K27Ac deposition at AP-1 binding sites that reflected the graded strength of TCR signaling.
source: There was an increase in H3K27Ac deposition at AP-1 binding sites that reflected the graded strength of TCR signaling (BATF shown in Figure 4H; other AP-1 family members in Figure 5—figure supplement 1H,I), indicating that AP-1 binding sites became more active in a graded manner corresponding to increasing TCR signaling.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 4H and Figure 5—figure supplement 1H,I.

claim: Most super-enhancers (approximately 450 out of 700 total) identified were shared by both the unstimulated and stimulated conditions.
source: Most super-enhancers (approximately 450 out of 700 total) identified were shared by both the unstimulated and stimulated conditions.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: GO analysis of genes nearby the shared super-enhancers showed enrichment for leukocyte activation genes as well as Pleckstrin homology genes.
source: GO analysis of genes nearby the shared super-enhancers showed enrichment for leukocyte activation genes as well as Pleckstrin homology genes, which are critical components of a number of kinase signaling pathways downstream of the TCR (Figure 6A), indicating that super-enhancers in CD4+ T cells prime genes important for inflammatory signaling.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Even though many of the super-enhancers exist prior to stimulation, super-enhancers near activation signature genes show an increase in H3K27Ac signal subsequent to TCR signaling.
source: Notably, even though many of the super-enhancers exist prior to stimulation, super-enhancers near activation signature genes show an increase in H3K27Ac signal subsequent to TCR signaling (Figure 6D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 118 of the 568 super-enhancers identified after TCR stimulation were not identified as super-enhancers in the unstimulated condition.
source: 118 of the 568 super-enhancers identified after TCR stimulation were not identified as super-enhancers in the unstimulated condition.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 6.

claim: The super-enhancers that required TCR signaling were enriched for leukocyte activation genes crucial for T cell activation.
source: The super-enhancers that required TCR signaling were enriched for leukocyte activation genes (Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value = 4.6e-7) crucial for T cell activation, including Batf (Figure 6E), Il2ra (CD25, Figure 6F), Tbx21 (Tbet, Figure 6G), Lag3 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), and Stat5b (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The amount of p-ERK in the p-ERK+ cells varied on a per-cell basis in each condition, increasing with TCR signal strength.
source: We first compared the level of phosphorylated ERK (p-ERK) in each condition using flow cytometry, and found that, like CD69 and CD25, the amount of p-ERK in the p-ERK+ cells varied on a per-cell basis in each condition, increasing with TCR signal strength (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Activation signature genes showed a significantly higher frequency of AP-1 binding compared to the bottom 10% of PC1 genes.
source: As the increasing levels of p-ERK paralleled the general pattern of expression of the activation signature genes, we assessed binding frequencies of AP-1 factors in the gene promoters of the activation signature genes as compared to the bottom 10% of PC1 genes, and found that activation signature genes showed a significantly higher frequency of AP-1 binding (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: MEK inhibition decreased the levels of the extracellular signaling marker CD69.
source: Low-dose MEK inhibition decreased the levels of the extracellular signaling marker CD69 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), which was in the top 10% of PC1, but this suppression was not universal, as CD4, an example of a gene not in the top 10% of PC1, was not significantly affected (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MEK inhibition at IC50 decreased expression of activation signature genes.
source: Accordingly, MEK inhibition at IC50 decreased expression of activation signature genes (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 1E), but, as with extracellular expression of CD69, this effect was selective; expression of genes in the bottom 10% was increased or unchanged (Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7C, Figure 7D, Figure 7—figure supplement 1E, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Using the activation score to assess total T cell activation status, MEKi shifted each sample down in score.
source: Using the activation score to assess total T cell activation status, we found that MEKi shifted each sample down in score (Figure 7E), as would be expected if the graded levels of pERK seen with each condition were prescriptive of the activation status of the condition.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Graded levels of pERK downstream of the TCR help to translate the analog activation signal to graded levels of enhancer activity and gene expression genome-wide.
source: Thus, graded levels of pERK downstream of the TCR help to translate the analog activation signal to graded levels of enhancer activity and gene expression genome-wide (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: On a per-cell basis, stronger TCR signals result in higher levels of phosphorylated ERK, a proportional increase in enhancer acetylation, and quantitative increases in activation markers such as CD69 and CD25.
source: Here, we have shown that the traditional model of a purely digital TCR response is too simple; on a per-cell basis, stronger TCR signals result in higher levels of phosphorylated ERK, a proportional increase in enhancer acetylation, and quantitative increases in activation markers such as CD69 and CD25 (Figure 7F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Varying the dose or the affinity of the pMHC-TCR interaction results in a gene expression profile that is graded corresponding to increasing strength of TCR signaling.
source: As a result of both these single-cell differences and the increasing frequency of respondent cells, varying the dose or the affinity of the pMHC-TCR interaction results in a gene expression profile that is graded corresponding to increasing strength of TCR signaling.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Dose and affinity are not interpreted separately downstream of the TCR, but rather overall signaling strength sets the level of activation across the population.
source: Notably, the predominance of PC1 and the graded gene expression patterns together indicate that dose and affinity are not interpreted separately downstream of the TCR, but rather overall signaling strength sets the level of activation across the population.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 2.

claim: The CD4+ T cell enhancer landscape is largely pre-established, with subsets of H3K4me2-marked enhancers increasing in activity, but little in the way of de novo enhancer establishment.
source: While it remains to be seen whether non-TCR signaling pathways or polarizing conditions induce more dramatic changes, the data presented here indicates that the CD4+ T cell enhancer landscape is largely pre-established, with subsets of H3K4me2-marked enhancers increasing in activity, but little in the way of de novo enhancer establishment.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5 and Table 1.

claim: If all enhancers are primed basally, and many are even activated basally, then pro-inflammatory transcription factors can bind at established enhancers and initiate new gene expression programs with minimal additional transcriptional machinery.
source: This finding helps to explain the speed and plasticity of the CD4+ T cell response (Zhou et al., 2009)—if all enhancers are primed basally, and many are even activated basally, then pro-inflammatory transcription factors can bind at established enhancers and initiate new gene expression programs with minimal additional transcriptional machinery.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5 and Figure 6, with a citation to published work.

claim: The graded levels of pERK in CD4+ T cells prove important for downstream enhancer and gene activity.
source: The graded levels of pERK in CD4+ T cells prove important for downstream enhancer and gene activity.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Low-dose MEK inhibition selectively decreased expression of the activation signature genes such that the activation score under the inhibited conditions was incrementally decreased.
source: Low-dose MEK inhibition selectively decreased expression of the activation signature genes such that the activation score under the inhibited conditions was incrementally decreased.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: The analog levels of pERK seen on a per-cell basis are translated at a population level into increased enhancer and gene activity.
source: This indicates that the analog levels of pERK seen on a per-cell basis are translated at a population level into increased enhancer and gene activity, and that 'turning down' pERK levels selectively diminishes the activation status of the cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: Low-dose ERK pathway inhibition could be used to selectively decrease the activity of activation signature genes in CD4+ T cells, achieving low-level immunosuppression without killing T cells or completely removing their ability to respond to TCR signaling.
source: Our findings suggest that low-dose ERK pathway inhibition could be used to selectively decrease the activity of activation signature genes in CD4+ T cells, achieving low-level immunosuppression without killing T cells or completely removing their ability to respond to TCR signaling.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 7.

claim: The effect of MEK inhibitors on CD4+ T cells raises questions about the immunosuppressive effects of using MEK inhibitors in cancer treatment, especially as current clinical trials combine MEK inhibitors with checkpoint-blockade inhibitors.
source: Further, the effect of MEK inhibitors on CD4+ T cells raises questions about the immunosuppressive effects of using MEK inhibitors in cancer treatment, especially as current clinical trials combine MEK inhibitors with checkpoint-blockade inhibitors (Zhao and Adjei, 2014; Vella et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 7, with citations to published work.

claim: Analog levels of pERK within the context of digital TCR signaling flow downstream to result in graded gene expression profiles and enhancer landscapes that can be used to characterize CD4+ T cell signaling at large.
source: In sum, this study makes use of a unique model system to dissect the transcriptional responses of CD4+ T cells to increasing strength of signaling, and demonstrates that analog levels of pERK within the context of digital TCR signaling flow downstream to result in graded gene expression profiles and enhancer landscapes that can be used to characterize CD4+ T cell signaling at large.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: High-affinity interactions lead to inflammatory responses at a lower concentration of antigen, increased Interleukin 2 (IL2) and IFNγ production, and increased proliferation.
source: Even small differences in the number or affinity of these pMHC-TCR interactions are read by the TCR and have important consequences for the nature and extent CD4+ T cell activation; high-affinity interactions lead to inflammatory responses at a lower concentration of antigen, increased Interleukin 2 (IL2) and IFNγ production, and increased proliferation (Heber-Katz et al., 1982; Hedrick et al., 1982; Solinger et al., 1979; Alexander, 1993; Rogers and Peptide dose, 1999; Rogers et al., 1998; Sloan-Lancaster et al., 1993; Tubo et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: Lower affinity interactions can lead to incomplete phosphorylation of downstream signaling complexes, anergy, or TCR antagonism.
source: whereas lower affinity interactions can lead to incomplete phosphorylation of downstream signaling complexes (Kersh et al., 1998b; Sloan-Lancaster et al., 1994), anergy (Sloan-Lancaster et al., 1993, 1994), or TCR antagonism (Alexander, 1993; Kersh et al., 1998b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: TCR responses have been characterized as digital—that is, signaling downstream of the TCR is either all-on or all-off, such that a given T cell must either be committed to a full response or to no response.
source: TCR responses have been characterized as digital (Coward et al., 2010)—that is, signaling downstream of the TCR is either all-on or all-off, such that a given T cell must either be committed to a full response or to no response.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Previous work has established switch-like behavior as observable in terms of extracellular markers such as CD69, ERK pathway component localization, NF-κB activation, NFAT localization, cell-cycle entry, and cytokine production.
source: Previous work has established this switch-like behavior as observable in terms of extracellular markers such as CD69 (Das et al., 2009; Daniels et al., 2006), ERK pathway component localization (Das et al., 2009; Daniels et al., 2006; Prasad et al., 2009), NF-κB activation (Kingeter et al., 2010), NFAT localization (Marangoni et al., 2013; Podtschaske et al., 2007), cell-cycle entry (Au-Yeung et al., 2014), and cytokine production (Podtschaske et al., 2007; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: Some aspects of the TCR response have been described as analog, or varying in proportion to the strength of signaling: CD3ζ chain phosphorylation; Zap70 activation; intracellular calcium concentrations; expression of the transcription factor IRF4; and cell division time.
source: Still, some aspects of the TCR response have been described as analog, or varying in proportion to the strength of signaling: CD3ζ chain phosphorylation (Kersh et al., 1998a; Sloan-Lancaster et al., 1994; Daniels et al., 2006; Kersh et al., 1999; Kersh et al., 1998a); Zap70 activation (Daniels et al., 2006; Prasad et al., 2009); intracellular calcium concentrations (Irvine et al., 2002); expression of the transcription factor IRF4 (Man et al., 2013; Nayar, 2014); and cell division time (Marchingo, 2014).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: At least four feedback loops have been identified in thymocytes and peripheral T cells downstream of the TCR.
source: At least four feedback loops have been identified in thymocytes and peripheral T cells downstream of the TCR (Coward et al., 2010; Feinerman et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to published work.

claim: Feedback loops downstream of the TCR serve to enforce a digital response by either dampening sub-threshold signaling or amplifying above-threshold signaling, resulting in T cell responses that are all-off or all-on, respectively.
source: Collectively, these feedback loops serve to enforce a digital response by either dampening sub-threshold signaling or amplifying above-threshold signaling, resulting in T cell responses that are all-off or all-on, respectively.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the citations to published work.

claim: The great majority of naïve CD4+ T cells extracted from AND mouse spleens expressed the V alpha 11 chain and the V beta 3 chain.
source: The AND mouse TCR includes the V alpha 11 chain and the V beta 3 chain. The great majority of naïve CD4+ T cells extracted from AND mouse spleens expressed this pair of TCR chains.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: APCs for peptide presentation were extracted from mouse spleens using positive selection for CD11c.
source: APCs for peptide presentation were extracted from mouse spleens using positive selection for CD11c. The extracted cells were largely positive for both CD11c and MHC class II molecules.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: At promoters, H3K4me2 marks were shared across the five conditions, but activation signature genes showed spreading of the H3K4me2 mark along the body of the gene after TCR stimulation.
source: At promoters, H3K4me2 marks were shared across the five conditions, but activation signature genes showed spreading of the H3K4me2 mark along the body of the gene after TCR stimulation. In contrast, H3K4me2 peaks were narrow and focal for the untreated condition at many of these genes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: The process of activating activation signature genes subsequent to TCR stimulation induces deposition of the dimethyl mark along the body of the genes as they are transcribed.
source: This implies that the process of activating these genes subsequent to TCR stimulation induces deposition of the dimethyl mark along the body of the genes as they are transcribed.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-D.

claim: Frequency of pERK+ cells differed across peptide conditions.
source: Frequency of pERK+ cells also differed across peptide conditions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), indicating that both frequency and single-cell response level play a role in the effect of MEK inhibitors.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: MEK inhibitor treatment at 0.5 μM (IC50) results in the preferential reduction of activation signature genes.
source: MEK inhibitor treatment at 0.5 μM (IC50) results in the preferential reduction of activation signature genes. CD69, one of the activation signature genes, reflects this decrease in expression level at the protein level, as measured by extracellular flow cytometry.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: CD4 does not show a change in expression level upon treatment with the MEK inhibitor.
source: In contrast to CD69, CD4 does not show a change in expression level upon treatment with the MEK inhibitor.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: TNF and IL2 are members of the 'digital' class of RNAs identified in CD69+ cells.
source: Our findings are consistent with these earlier studies in that TNF and IL2 are members of the 'digital' class of RNAs identified in CD69+ cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The increase in expression of genes involved in protein expression could at least partly explain the observation that the rates of TNF and IL2 protein production are increased in blasts and memory cells in comparison to naïve cells.
source: Furthermore, the increase in expression of genes involved in protein expression revealed by the present studies could at least partly explain the observation that the rates of TNF and IL2 protein production are increased in blasts and memory cells in comparison to naïve cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 2 and Figure 3.

claim: The analogue increase in protein biosynthetic machinery could also at least partly explain the observation that CD69 expression is digital at the level of mRNA but analogue at the level of protein expression.
source: The analogue increase in protein biosynthetic machinery could also at least partly explain the observation that CD69 expression is digital at the level of mRNA but analogue at the level of protein expression (Figure 1A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and is based on the data presented in Figure 1A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.
